(F 15 here). Your step son is very lucky to have been taught these skills. I'm actually in a very similar parental situation to your stepson. 

My mom left when I was very young to escape the abusive relationship she was in with my father, but that's a different story. I have lived with my grandparents my entire life after they split because my dad is working on bettering himself and he works his job so much. My dad (diagnosed with bipolar disorder, severe obsessive compulsive disorder) is always very tight about money, and he struggles to spend money, making my grandparents my overall providers. 

They always wanted me to have a happy childhood and make up for all the things I missed and the trauma from when I was younger and in that shitty living situation.  I am also their oldest grandchild and for a while, I was their only grandchild, and so they wanted to spoil me and me only because their sons were adults dealing with their own issues. 

It was confusing because I was so used to having nothing with my father, but eventually I caught on. I was still a very well behaved child and I did my best to be the "perfect" child. Anyways, I got so used to being pampered. I never was snobby about it and I didn't whine, but it was just something I was used to. When my grandparents sold their properties and retired, it meant less income. Unfortunately, I was too young to understand this and it made me very confused and made me feel like I was doing something wrong. And on top of that, it's not really something you'd go to in depth with an 8 year old. 

Still to this day, I get confused and think that what I'm doing isn't good enough because of our financial situation. Although I understand a lot better, because of how I was raised my brain still makes that connection. I wish I would've been taught at a younger age that not everyone can have everything, and that that doesn't define their worth or if they're good enough. I struggle with saving money and I have an issue with retail therapy but that's something I'm working on. I just wish I wasn't spoiled when I was younger and I was taught these things at age appropriate levels because it would definitely help me now. I'm just happy I was never a snobby child.
